claims.statement: Consorts of successive ancestral generations (累代祖妣) shared in founding labor

translationRepairs: The imperial great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, was plain and honest by nature and a moral beacon for the people; expert in mounted archery, he went forth and nothing stood before him; when he first appointed officials and teachers, ever more tribes came to submit.

The imperial great-great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, was plain and honest by nature and a moral beacon for the people; expert in mounted archery, he went forth and nothing stood before him; when he first appointed officials and teachers, ever more tribes came to submit.
Focus unit 皇高祖太師 sits above 皇曾祖 in the ancestral ladder (六代祖–五代祖–高祖–曾祖); 高祖 is the fourth-generation ancestor, i.e. great-great-grandfather, not great-grandfather.

The imperial great-great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, whose authority and majesty shook distant lands and whose alertness surpassed all others, excelled in strategy and never took the field lightly clad in armor; facing the enemy he fought all the harder, adapting to change like a spirit.

The imperial great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, whose authority and majesty shook distant lands and whose alertness surpassed all others, excelled in strategy and never took the field lightly clad in armor; facing the enemy he fought all the harder, adapting to change like a spirit.
Focus unit 皇曾祖太師 follows 皇高祖 and precedes 皇曾叔祖/皇伯祖; 曾祖 is great-grandfather. Calling him great-great-grandfather overstates the generation by one.

The imperial great-great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, whose designs sprang from the heart alone and whose public service knew no private gain, stirred the four quarters until every tribe returned in allegiance; virtue and awe alike rose high, and customs were greatly settled.

The imperial great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, whose designs sprang from the heart alone and whose public service knew no private gain, stirred the four quarters until every tribe returned in allegiance; virtue and awe alike rose high, and customs were greatly settled.
Focus unit 皇曾叔祖太師 is the brother-generation of 皇曾祖; 曾叔祖 is great-granduncle, not great-great-granduncle.

Hui is for loving the people and delighting in giving, huan for opening territory and uniting states, zhao for illustrious virtue with meritorious toil, su for firm resolve and decisive judgment—we ask that the imperial great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Huihuan, with the temple name Jingzu, and that his consort be titled Empress Zhaosu.

Hui is for loving the people and delighting in giving, huan for opening territory and uniting states, zhao for illustrious virtue with meritorious toil, su for firm resolve and decisive judgment—we ask that the imperial great-great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Huihuan, with the temple name Jingzu, and that his consort be titled Empress Zhaosu.
Title request 請上皇高祖太師尊諡 repeats the same 皇高祖 as s0018; great-great-grandfather is required here as well.

Sheng is for great transformation of all under Heaven, su for firm virtue brought to completion, yi for deep thought and far-reaching consideration, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening—we ask that the imperial great-great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Shengsu, with the temple name Shizu, and that his consort be titled Empress Yijian.

Sheng is for great transformation of all under Heaven, su for firm virtue brought to completion, yi for deep thought and far-reaching consideration, jian for single-minded virtue without slackening—we ask that the imperial great-grandfather, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Shengsu, with the temple name Shizu, and that his consort be titled Empress Yijian.
Title request 請上皇曾祖太師尊諡 matches s0019’s 皇曾祖; the idiomatic great-great-grandfather wrongly labels 曾祖.

Mu is for expressing feeling and revealing true character, xian for broad learning and many abilities, jing for gentle virtue and love of the multitude, xuan for sagely goodness known throughout the realm—we ask that the imperial great-great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Muxian, with the temple name Suzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Jingxuan.

Mu is for expressing feeling and revealing true character, xian for broad learning and many abilities, jing for gentle virtue and love of the multitude, xuan for sagely goodness known throughout the realm—we ask that the imperial great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Muxian, with the temple name Suzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Jingxuan.
Title request 請上皇曾叔祖太師尊諡 uses 皇曾叔祖; great-granduncle is the correct English kinship term.

Xiao is for loving kindness that forgets fatigue, ping for conducting affairs with proper measure, zhen for pure integrity and guarding one's principles, hui for loving the people and delighting in giving—we ask that the imperial great-great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoping, with the temple name Muzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Zhenhui.

Xiao is for loving kindness that forgets fatigue, ping for conducting affairs with proper measure, zhen for pure integrity and guarding one's principles, hui for loving the people and delighting in giving—we ask that the imperial great-granduncle, Grand Preceptor, receive the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoping, with the temple name Muzong, and that his consort be titled Empress Zhenhui.
Same kinship term 皇曾叔祖 in the Muzong title request; great-granduncle restores the correct generation relative to 曾祖.
The relevant offices memorialized: 'Emperor Ruizong has not yet been enshrined in the main ancestral line; should a spirit couch and table be set up in the Shengwu Hall of Yanging Palace?'
The relevant offices memorialized: 'Emperor Ruizong has not yet been enshrined in the main ancestral line; should a spirit couch and table be set up in the Shengwu Hall of Yanqing Palace?'
Chinese 衍慶宮 is Yanqing Palace; Yanging is a misspelling of the pinyin for 慶 (qìng).
The day before, the registers and seals were escorted from Yanging Palace and installed in Da'an Hall.
The day before, the registers and seals were escorted from Yanqing Palace and installed in Da'an Hall.
Chinese 自衍慶宮 likewise requires Yanqing Palace, not Yanging.

On the first day of the tenth month, Acting Grand Mentor Wanyan Zongxian, Special Advancement Chief Councillor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Duke of Ding, led the officials to Yanging Palace to perform the rite.

On the first day of the tenth month, Acting Grand Mentor Wanyan Zongxian, Special Advancement Chief Councillor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Duke of Ding, led the officials to Yanqing Palace to perform the rite.
Chinese 赴衍慶宮行禮 names Yanqing Palace; the proposed spelling matches 衍慶.
The registers and seals were escorted to outside Yanging Palace; the Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Gatekeeper Service each bore them down from the carriage and placed them on the stands.
The registers and seals were escorted to outside Yanqing Palace; the Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Gatekeeper Service each bore them down from the carriage and placed them on the stands.
Chinese 至衍慶宮門外 again requires Yanqing; Yanging misrenders 慶.
